migration.description: Add Host-scoped Codex source snapshots, preserved protocol history and supported file materials while retaining legacy null-Host execution sessions and strengthening existing Host provenance to Host-scoped thread identity.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one Codex source discovery, history sharing and conversation title synchronization.

compatibility_assessment.reason: The migration adds new Codex source tables and makes execution-session source identity Host-scoped for new rows. Existing rows with NULL host_id remain readable and are never guessed into a Host.

durable_state.description: Source snapshots retain exact Host identity, source status, protocol build/capability evidence, full raw history events, supported file bytes or references, title synchronization state, and immutable Task/Session links.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL tables and indexes managed by the embedded Goose application migration history.

source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Codex source synchronization candidate containing migration 00022.
source_compatibility_range.compatibility_boundary: Older candidates can read legacy execution sessions but do not know the Codex source tables. After a new Host-scoped execution session or Codex binding is written, switchback requires the forward candidate because the old global external-thread uniqueness model is no longer the source contract.

ordered_operations.description: Reuse nullable Host provenance from migration 00010 and replace the global execution-session external-thread uniqueness with a Host-scoped partial unique index.
Create Host-scoped source, project, thread, mapping, link, history, file-material and snapshot tables with foreign keys and readiness indexes.

database_migration.backfill: none; legacy NULL-host execution sessions remain readable and source rows are populated only by explicit Codex synchronization.
rollout_signals: A source snapshot records an exact build and capability set, or an explicit unavailable state.
History events are deduplicated by Host/thread/event identity and file material is marked complete before a bound thread becomes project-visible.
Title operations preserve both values and pending, failed, conflict or paused state without silently rolling back a local title.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version; do not guess Host provenance for NULL-host rows

validation: Fresh and upgraded PostgreSQL databases apply migration 00022 with all Host-scoped foreign keys and partial indexes present.
An upgrade fixture containing legacy NULL-host execution sessions keeps those rows readable and does not create a guessed Host binding.
Repeated history delivery is idempotent and incomplete history/file materials keep a thread out of project-visible bindings.
